module_title: UP Wildlife & Reserves - Foundational Matrix (Core Parks and Extremes)
introduction: Uttar Pradesh has only one National Park but boasts a robust network of Tiger Reserves, Wildlife Sanctuaries, and Bird Parks. At this foundational level, we must memorize the single National Park, all 4 Tiger Reserves, and the absolute extremes (largest, smallest, oldest) that are guaranteed one-liner questions.

core_concepts.title: The Lone National Park
core_concepts.description: - **Dudhwa National Park:** Located primarily in the **Lakhimpur Kheri** district. It was elevated to National Park status in 1977 and is globally renowned for the conservation of the **Bengal Tiger** and the **Swamp Deer (Barasingha)**.

core_concepts.title: The 4 Tiger Reserves of UP
core_concepts.description:
Uttar Pradesh currently hosts exactly 4 Tiger Reserves:
1. **Dudhwa Tiger Reserve:** Lakhimpur Kheri (The oldest, declared in 1987-88).
2. **Amangarh Tiger Reserve:** Bijnor (Declared in 2012, it serves as a critical buffer zone to the Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand).
3. **Pilibhit Tiger Reserve:** Pilibhit (Declared in 2014, famous for winning the global 'TX2' award for doubling its tiger population).
4. **Ranipur Tiger Reserve:** Chitrakoot (Declared in late 2022, it is the state's **4th and newest** tiger reserve, and uniquely the first one in the Bundelkhand region).

core_concepts.title: Wildlife Sanctuaries (Extremes)
core_concepts.description:
- **First / Oldest:** Chandraprabha Wildlife Sanctuary (Chandauli, established 1957).
- **Largest:** Hastinapur Wildlife Sanctuary (Spread across a massive 2073 sq. km covering Meerut, Muzaffarnagar, Bijnor, and Amroha).
- **Smallest:** Mahavir Swami Wildlife Sanctuary (Lalitpur, covering just 5.4 sq. km).

core_concepts.title: Bird Sanctuaries (Extremes)
core_concepts.description:
- **First / Oldest:** Nawabganj Bird Sanctuary (Unnao, 1984). It has been officially renamed as *Shaheed Chandra Shekhar Azad Bird Sanctuary*.
- **Largest:** Lakh Bahoshi Bird Sanctuary (Kannauj, covering 80 sq. km).
- **Smallest:** Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary (Aligarh, ~0.4 sq km) and Patna Bird Sanctuary (Etah, ~1 sq. km).

important_entities.name: Ranipur Tiger Reserve
important_entities.significance: Notified in 2022 as India's 53rd tiger reserve, it is structurally significant because it established the first-ever protected tiger habitat in the arid Bundelkhand region, acting as a corridor for tigers moving from the Panna Tiger Reserve in Madhya Pradesh.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: This is the most infamous trap in UP exams. Upon reading 'Patna Bird Sanctuary', students reflexively mark Bihar as the location. However, it is located in the **Etah** district of Uttar Pradesh.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Kannauj is famous as the perfume (Ittar) capital of India, which is an expensive luxury. This links perfectly to the **Lakh Bahoshi** (Largest) Bird Sanctuary located there.

exam_strategy_tips: In basic state exams like UP Police and VDO, the 'Smallest/Largest' superlatives and the district for Ranipur Tiger Reserve (Chitrakoot) are heavily tested. Never forget that Dudhwa is in Lakhimpur Kheri.
